environment.note: The live worker was not stopped, so its changing GPU workload is an uncontrolled realistic-contention factor. All benchmark inputs were synthetic.

current_generate_and_grounding_check_equ.scope: Draft generation and grounding check only; excludes route/retrieval, queue wait, and UI delivery.

conclusion: Two 9B workers are memory-feasible and drain a backlog faster, but shared-GPU contention increases individual latency. Use an adaptive pool capped at two: one worker for a lone ready job and start the second only when at least two jobs are ready.
